disposition_8_6: SURVIVES AS A REPORTED REFERENCE MARK. RETIRED AS A GATE.
disposition_reasoning: K was calibrated to DECIDE. An axis fired when its IDF-weighted mass reached 2.431, and an axis that did not fire was REMOVED from the router output before anything downstream could see it. Sub-step 8.1 deletes the decision, so the only live question is whether the number is still worth reporting.

IT IS, AND THE EVIDENCE IS IN THIS FILE. The eleven rows under "fails" are the eleven probe questions where the plateau midpoint disagreed with the register author. Eleven of sixty-six at the best-scoring value -- one in six -- and they are not a tuning residue. LCC-07 misses its own probe_pos at 0.968 because the key reads "kwh" and the question reads "kilowatt hours". LCC-09 misses at 0.919 on "polar" against "pole". A mark whose own calibration record contains its own refutation is worth showing to a reader. It is not worth filtering on.

KEPT AS A REPORTED NUMBER, because a mass with no scale is unreadable. 1.540 means nothing alone; 1.540 against 2.431 is a near miss and 0.428 against 2.431 is not. The router now emits mass, mark, signed margin, and margin as a fraction of the mark, and derives a stated confidence from the last of those.

NOT WIDENED INTO A BAND. A band is still a gate: it decides three ways instead of two and the failure mode is unchanged -- a question near an edge receives a categorical answer the measurement does not support. The margin IS the band, reported continuously, and nobody has to choose its width.

THE PLATEAU IS THE HONEST SUMMARY OF THIS CALIBRATION AND IT ARGUES AGAINST ITSELF. The best-scoring interval is [2.3195, 2.5416]: 55 of 66, over a 9% wide plateau on which the score does not move at all. A quantity that any value in a 9% interval serves equally is not a quantity the answer depends on. It was carried as 2.431, to three decimal places, for two full seat-sittings.

THIS FILE IS RETAINED AS THE RECORD OF WHAT WAS MEASURED. It is still READ by oracle/router/classify.js, and only so that a margin can be computed. Deleting it makes the router report masses without margins; it does not make the router refuse, which is what it used to do.
set_by: oracle/router/calibrate_k.js, run by The Software Engineer at sub-step 3.8
retired_as_a_gate_at: sub-steps 8.1 and 8.6, The Software Engineer, on the author ruling of 2026-08-28
provenance: plateau midpoint of the widest best-scoring interval over the register's own probe_pos/probe_neg fixture set (oracle/register_schema.md section 4.2), 66 labelled questions over 33 axes
idf: field-scoped, oracle/retrieval/literature_search.js idfFor(), scoped to the axis's own register field
rule_now: reported. mass, mark, margin = mass - K, margin / K, and a stated confidence. Nothing is filtered, ranked out or suppressed by this number.
caveat: This is a measurement, not a ruling. 3.6 owns K. The classifier reads this file and refuses input-missing when it is absent rather than defaulting, so replacing this value is an edit to one artifact and touches no code.
fails_note: The eleven disagreements at the adopted value, kept verbatim. These are the argument for retiring the gate, not a defect list to be worked off.
